title: 1997 Transitions, Elbow Grids, Font-Made Spacing, A Hungry Delete & Holes in the Overlay
description: Five patterns that let the shape do the work: a mask, a radius, a font metric, a measured hop and a hole.

drops.title: Transitions From 1997
drops.description: Internet Explorer's RevealTrans effects — blinds, checkerboard, random bars, dissolve — rebuilt on the View Transition API.
drops.concept: IE 5.5 shipped twenty-four page transitions you declared in a meta tag, and every one of them was a mask or a clip. The View Transition API hands you the same two tools: here three panels swap inside a single startViewTransition(), each with its own view-transition-name, so three different effects run at once on ::view-transition-new().

interaction.mouse: Pick an effect per panel, drag duration, blind size and checker cell
interaction.click: Next page runs all three at once; shuffle or run the same effect ×3; auto-cycle
interaction.touch: Tap Next; the panels stack to one column

drops.title: The Elbow Grid
drops.description: LCARS in three numbers — a rail width, a sweep height and one radius generate the whole panel language.
drops.concept: The Star Trek console has outlived every interface it was drawn against because it is structural, not decorative. The corner that welds the vertical rail to the horizontal sweep is a single block: an outer border-radius plus a notch cut by a pseudo-element painted in the page colour, sized calc(100% - var(--rail)) by calc(100% - var(--bar)) so it can never drift out of alignment.

interaction.mouse: Drag rail width, sweep height, radius, gutter and palette rotation
interaction.click: Pick a rail segment; toggle the rail guide lines
interaction.touch: Tap the rail segments; the console reflows at phone width

drops.title: Spacing That Comes From the Font
drops.description: calc(1lh - 1ex) measures the channel a reader actually sees, so every margin re-measures when the typeface changes.
drops.concept: Design systems pick 8px and hope. The gap a reader perceives is baseline-to-baseline minus x-height, and CSS can express exactly that. Trim the half-leading with text-box: trim-both, derive --gap from the element's own metrics, and three typefaces sharing one stylesheet each space themselves correctly.

interaction.mouse: Drag line-height, base size and specimen scale; watch the measured gap update per column
interaction.click: Toggle text-box trimming, the gap bands, and a fixed 8px module to compare
interaction.touch: Columns stack; the measured gaps stay live

drops.title: The Button Eats Its Own Label
drops.description: Letters hop into the bin, the pill folds to a circle, and a ring spends the undo window inside the control.
drops.concept: Destructive actions usually confirm somewhere else — a modal, a toast, a second button. This keeps the whole transaction in the control: each letter is measured at click time so it lands in the bin wherever the pill sits, then a conic-gradient ring counts the undo window down. Click again and the letters hop back out.

interaction.mouse: Drag letter stagger, hop height, undo window and pill width
interaction.click: Delete to start it, the circle again to undo, Restore to bring rows back
interaction.touch: Tap Delete; the rows and rings work the same

drops.title: A Spotlight You Can Click Through
drops.description: A product tour that cuts holes in its own overlay, so the real control underneath keeps its clicks and its keyboard.
drops.concept: Most tours drop a transparent div over the app and swallow every click. Cut the hole instead: each target becomes a mask layer composited with mask-composite: exclude, and the overlay keeps pointer-events: none. A step can light several targets at once, guard itself with a validator, and anchor its message with CSS anchor positioning.

interaction.mouse: Drag dim, hole padding and feather; toggle blocking mode
interaction.click: Start the tour, then type, select and toggle the real app through the overlay; Next guards on step 3
interaction.touch: Tap through the steps; the message card flips below the cutout
